correctness.rationale: For any 4-word there are exactly three deletion scripts, hence <=3 distinct outputs and |C|>=ceil(q²/3). Every seven recorded rectangular template has three distinct output cells per word and directly covers its whole rectangle, with only the 2x2 and 4x4 templates having precisely two double-incidence cells. Partitioning both alphabet axes into 3-blocks plus a terminal 2-block (q mod3=2) or 4-block (q mod3=1) leaves exactly one exceptional square. Counting codewords yields q²/3 when 3|q and (q²+2)/3 otherwise, which equals ceil(q²/3); duplicate codewords across rectangles are excluded by block membership. Embedded verify.py checks every template and generated q=2..100; no infinite quantifier depends on finite computation.

value.rationale: This resolves the complete first nontrivial adjacent-two-deletion covering capacity across every alphabet, with a sharp volume bound attained for every q and exact-output partitions when 3|q. That precisely benchmarkable quantity matters because earlier nonbinary burst-deletion code constructions had only weaker general-size guarantees (e.g. 8 instead of optimum 6 for q=4); the reusable incidence-grid tiling mechanism supplies a concrete O(q²)-output constructive design. It is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a mere recomputation of a known table; length four is the first source size with three possible adjacent deletion positions, and every q is covered.
